### 10.2.2 Tornado plot

A tornado of the incremental NMB (transplant − dialysis) is the more useful plot, so we build it directly from the OWSA results below.

```{r tornado-incremental}
# OWSA results in long format: parameter, strategy, param_val, outcome_val (NMB)
df_owsa <- as.data.frame(owsa_nmb)
v_str_owsa <- unique(df_owsa$strategy)          # strategy labels as stored by run_owsa_det()
                                                # (dialysis first, transplant second)
# One row per parameter value, one column per strategy
df_owsa_w <- tidyr::pivot_wider(df_owsa[, c("parameter", "param_val", "strategy", "outcome_val")],
                                names_from = strategy, values_from = outcome_val)
# Incremental NMB of transplant vs dialysis at each parameter value
df_owsa_w$inc_nmb <- df_owsa_w[[v_str_owsa[2]]] - df_owsa_w[[v_str_owsa[1]]]

# Base-case incremental NMB (about 315,626)
n_inc_nmb_base <- df_ce$NMB[2] - df_ce$NMB[1]

# For each parameter: incremental NMB at the lowest and highest value tested
df_tornado <- df_owsa_w %>%
  group_by(parameter) %>%
  summarise(low  = inc_nmb[which.min(param_val)],
            high = inc_nmb[which.max(param_val)],
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(width = abs(high - low)) %>%
  arrange(width) %>%
  mutate(parameter = factor(parameter, levels = parameter))   # widest bar at the top

# Long format: one bar from the base case to the low value, one to the high value
df_tornado_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(df_tornado, cols = c(low, high),
                                       names_to = "Level", values_to = "inc_nmb")
df_tornado_long$Level <- factor(df_tornado_long$Level, levels = c("low", "high"),
                                labels = c("Low value", "High value"))

gg_tornado <- ggplot(df_tornado_long) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = n_inc_nmb_base, xend = inc_nmb,
                   y = parameter, yend = parameter, colour = Level),
               linewidth = 6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = n_inc_nmb_base, linetype = "dashed") +   # base case
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "red") +                     # transplant and dialysis equal
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Low value" = "#1F7A8C", "High value" = "#E08E0B")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(x = "Incremental NMB, transplant vs dialysis ($50,000/QALY)",
       y = NULL, colour = "Parameter value") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
gg_tornado
# Dashed line = base case. Red line = 0: a bar crossing it would mean dialysis
# becomes preferred. No bar crosses it; dialysis cost (c_dial) has the widest bar.
df_tornado[order(-df_tornado$width), ]   # the numbers behind the plot

# Alternative: with the GitHub version of dampack
# (remotes::install_github("DARTH-git/dampack")) the built-in function plots the
# incremental NMB directly:
# owsa_tornado(owsa = owsa_nmb, select_str = v_names_str, outcome_name = "NMB")
```



### 10.2.3 One-way sensitivity table and threshold analysis (addition)

Here we wanted tro find out, how far would each input have to move before the decision flips to dialysis. 

```{r threshold-analysis}
n_wtp_thr <- 50000   # $ per QALY

# Readable labels for tables and plots
v_par_labels <- c(
  r_dial_exc             = "Extra death rate on dialysis (/year)",
  hr_early               = "HR of death, graft months 1-3 vs dialysis",
  r_GL_y1                = "Graft-loss rate, months 1-12 (/year)",
  r_G_exc                = "Extra death rate with a graft, month 4+ (/year)",
  r_GL_y2p               = "Graft-loss rate, month 13+ (/year)",
  p_GL_dead_annual       = "Death in first year after graft loss",
  u_dial                 = "Utility, dialysis",
  early_utility_fraction = "Utility gain in graft months 1-3 (fraction)",
  u_graft                = "Utility, functioning graft",
  c_dial                 = "Cost of dialysis (/month)",
  c_G1to3                = "Cost, graft months 1-3 (/month)",
  c_G4to12               = "Cost, graft months 4-12 (/month)",
  c_G13p                 = "Cost, graft month 13+ (/month)",
  c_tx_once              = "Cost of transplant (one-time)",
  d_c                    = "Discount rate, costs",
  d_e                    = "Discount rate, QALYs",
  n_cycles               = "Time horizon (months)")

# Incremental NMB (transplant - dialysis) with ONE parameter changed
f_inc_nmb <- function(par, val) {
  l <- l_params_all
  l[[par]] <- val
  ce <- calculate_ce_out(l, n_wtp = n_wtp_thr)
  ce$NMB[2] - ce$NMB[1]
}

# Values each parameter can logically take (where the threshold is searched)
f_domain <- function(par, base) {
  if (grepl("^c_", par))                                  return(c(0, 50 * base))
  if (grepl("^u_|^p_|^early_utility_fraction$", par))     return(c(1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))
  if (grepl("^r_", par))                                  return(c(1e-6, 2))
  if (par == "hr_early")                                  return(c(0.05, 20))
  if (par %in% c("d_c", "d_e"))                           return(c(0, 0.10))
  stop("No search domain for ", par)
}

# Threshold: evaluate on a grid of 25 values, find where the sign changes,
# then solve exactly with uniroot(). NA = the decision never changes.
f_threshold <- function(par) {
  base <- l_params_all[[par]]
  dom  <- f_domain(par, base)
  v_x  <- seq(dom[1], dom[2], length.out = 25)
  v_y  <- vapply(v_x, function(x) f_inc_nmb(par, x), numeric(1))
  k    <- which(diff(sign(v_y)) != 0)
  if (length(k) == 0) return(c(threshold = NA, dom_lo = dom[1], dom_hi = dom[2]))
  k    <- k[which.min(abs(v_x[k] - base))]          # crossing closest to the base case
  root <- uniroot(function(x) f_inc_nmb(par, x), lower = v_x[k], upper = v_x[k + 1],
                  tol = 1e-6 * max(1, abs(base)))$root
  c(threshold = root, dom_lo = dom[1], dom_hi = dom[2])
}

v_pars_thr <- setdiff(df_owsa_lit$pars, "n_cycles")   # horizon handled below
m_thr <- t(vapply(v_pars_thr, f_threshold, numeric(3)))

df_thr <- data.frame(
  pars        = v_pars_thr,
  Parameter   = unname(v_par_labels[v_pars_thr]),
  Base        = df_owsa_lit$base[match(v_pars_thr, df_owsa_lit$pars)],
  Range_low   = df_owsa_lit$min [match(v_pars_thr, df_owsa_lit$pars)],
  Range_high  = df_owsa_lit$max [match(v_pars_thr, df_owsa_lit$pars)],
  IncNMB_low  = df_tornado$low  [match(v_pars_thr, as.character(df_tornado$parameter))],
  IncNMB_high = df_tornado$high [match(v_pars_thr, as.character(df_tornado$parameter))],
  Threshold   = m_thr[, "threshold"],
  Dom_low     = m_thr[, "dom_lo"],
  Dom_high    = m_thr[, "dom_hi"])

# Time horizon: shortest horizon (even months) from which transplant stays cost-effective
v_h     <- seq(2, 60, by = 2)
v_h_nmb <- vapply(v_h, function(h) f_inc_nmb("n_cycles", h), numeric(1))
n_breakeven_h <- if (all(v_h_nmb > 0)) 2 else v_h[max(which(v_h_nmb <= 0)) + 1]
n_breakeven_h        # expected about 20 months (incremental NMB < 0 at 18, > 0 at 20)
df_thr <- rbind(df_thr, data.frame(
  pars = "n_cycles", Parameter = v_par_labels[["n_cycles"]], Base = n_cycles,
  Range_low = 60, Range_high = n_cycles,
  IncNMB_low  = df_tornado$low [as.character(df_tornado$parameter) == "n_cycles"],
  IncNMB_high = df_tornado$high[as.character(df_tornado$parameter) == "n_cycles"],
  Threshold = n_breakeven_h, Dom_low = 2, Dom_high = n_cycles))

# Formatting
f_fmt <- function(par, x) ifelse(grepl("^c_", par), scales::dollar(round(x)),
                          ifelse(par == "n_cycles", as.character(round(x)), as.character(signif(x, 3))))
df_thr$Within_range <- !is.na(df_thr$Threshold) &
                       df_thr$Threshold >= df_thr$Range_low & df_thr$Threshold <= df_thr$Range_high
df_thr$Dialysis_preferred_if <- ifelse(
  is.na(df_thr$Threshold),
  paste0("Never (searched ", f_fmt(df_thr$pars, df_thr$Dom_low), " to ", f_fmt(df_thr$pars, df_thr$Dom_high), ")"),
  ifelse(df_thr$Threshold < df_thr$Base,
         paste0("< ", f_fmt(df_thr$pars, df_thr$Threshold)),
         paste0("> ", f_fmt(df_thr$pars, df_thr$Threshold))))

df_thr_table <- data.frame(
  Parameter                   = df_thr$Parameter,
  `Base case`                 = f_fmt(df_thr$pars, df_thr$Base),
  `Range`                     = paste0(f_fmt(df_thr$pars, df_thr$Range_low), " - ", f_fmt(df_thr$pars, df_thr$Range_high)),
  `Inc. NMB at low`           = scales::dollar(round(df_thr$IncNMB_low)),
  `Inc. NMB at high`          = scales::dollar(round(df_thr$IncNMB_high)),
  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(df_thr_table, align = "lllrr",
             caption = paste0("One-way sensitivity analysis and threshold values (WTP $",
                              scales::comma(n_wtp_thr), "/QALY; base-case incremental NMB ",
                              scales::dollar(round(n_inc_nmb_base)), ")"))
# Expected thresholds: dialysis < $4,240/month; graft month 13+ > $8,125/month;
# graft months 4-12 > $47,314; graft months 1-3 > $156,375; transplant > $376,668;
# extra death rate on dialysis > 0.670/year (about 3% alive at 5 years on dialysis);
# horizon < 20 months. No other clinical parameter or utility changes the decision.
```

```{r}
df_thr_table <- data.frame(
  Input       = df_thr$Parameter,
  `Base case` = f_fmt(df_thr$pars, df_thr$Base),
  Range       = paste0(f_fmt(df_thr$pars, df_thr$Range_low), " - ", f_fmt(df_thr$pars, df_thr$Range_high)),
  Threshold   = ifelse(is.na(df_thr$Threshold),
                       "-",
                       ifelse(df_thr$Threshold < df_thr$Base,
                              paste0("< ", f_fmt(df_thr$pars, df_thr$Threshold)),
                              paste0("> ", f_fmt(df_thr$pars, df_thr$Threshold)))),
  check.names = FALSE)

knitr::kable(df_thr_table, align = "llll",
             caption = paste0("One-way sensitivity analysis: base case, literature range and threshold at which ",
                              "continued dialysis becomes preferred (WTP $", scales::comma(n_wtp_thr),
                              "/QALY; base-case incremental NMB ", scales::dollar(round(n_inc_nmb_base)), ")"))
```


```{r threshold-curves, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6}
## Plot 2: one-way curves for the parameters that have a threshold
# (as in the lecture, slide 60): incremental NMB across values of the
# parameter; shaded = literature range; red line = 0 (decision changes);
# dashed line = threshold; dot = base case.
df_thr_yes <- subset(df_thr, !is.na(Threshold) & pars != "n_cycles")
if (nrow(df_thr_yes) > 0) {
  df_curves <- do.call(rbind, lapply(df_thr_yes$pars, function(p) {
    r <- df_thr_yes[df_thr_yes$pars == p, ]
    v_x <- seq(0.8 * min(r$Range_low, r$Threshold), 1.2 * max(r$Range_high, r$Threshold), length.out = 30)
    data.frame(Parameter = r$Parameter, x = v_x,
               inc_nmb = vapply(v_x, function(v) f_inc_nmb(p, v), numeric(1)))
  }))
  df_thr_yes$base_nmb <- n_inc_nmb_base
  gg_thr_curves <- ggplot(df_curves, aes(x = x, y = inc_nmb)) +
    geom_rect(data = df_thr_yes, inherit.aes = FALSE,
              aes(xmin = Range_low, xmax = Range_high, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
              fill = "#1F7A8C", alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#C0392B") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_vline(data = df_thr_yes, aes(xintercept = Threshold), linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(data = df_thr_yes, aes(x = Base, y = base_nmb), size = 2.5) +
    facet_wrap(~ Parameter, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)) +   # costs and rates share this axis style
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
    labs(x = "Parameter value", y = "Incremental NMB, transplant vs dialysis",
         title = "One-way threshold analysis (parameters with a threshold)") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11)
  gg_thr_curves
}

## Plot 3: time horizon
gg_thr_h <- ggplot(data.frame(h = c(v_h, n_cycles), nmb = c(v_h_nmb, n_inc_nmb_base)), aes(h, nmb)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#C0392B") +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = n_breakeven_h, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = n_breakeven_h, y = max(v_h_nmb), hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5,
           label = paste0("Transplant cost-effective from a ", n_breakeven_h, "-month horizon")) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 62)) +
```

### 10.3.2 TWSA with wider ranges to show the threshold

```{r twsa-wide, results='hide'}
# Break-even: dialysis about $4,240/month at base graft cost ($3,272);
# graft cost about $8,125/month at base dialysis cost ($8,929).
df_params_twsa_wide <- data.frame(pars = c("c_dial", "c_G13p"),
                                  min  = c(2000,     1500),
                                  max  = c(12500,    9000))
twsa_nmb_wide <- run_twsa_det(params_range    = df_params_twsa_wide,
                              params_basecase = l_params_all,
                              nsamp           = 40,
                              FUN             = calculate_ce_out,
                              outcomes        = "NMB",
                              strategies      = v_names_str,
                              n_wtp           = 50000)
```

```{r}
plot(twsa_nmb_wide) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = v_twsa_fill, labels = v_twsa_lab, drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Dialysis cost per month ($)",
       y = "Graft follow-up cost per month, month 13+ ($)",
       fill = "Strategy") +
  annotate("point", x = l_params_all$c_dial, y = l_params_all$c_G13p,
           shape = 4, size = 4, stroke = 1.5)   # base case
```

# **11 Probabilistic Sensitivity Analysis (PSA)**

## 11.1 Model input

Here we used SE from CI or 10% of mean base values to calculate scale and shape for PSA. Beta distribution was used to make values between 0 and 1. Gamma distirbution was used for parameters that can take values from 0 to infinity. 

```{r}
# Store the parameter names into a vector
v_names_params <- names(l_params_all)

## Test functions to generate CE outcomes and PSA dataset 
# Test function to compute CE outcomes
calculate_ce_out(l_params_all) 

# PSA distributions, standard errors and their basis (method of moments)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "-")

knitr::kable(get_sa_spec(l_params_all)[, c("pars", "mean", "se", "distribution", "shape", "scale", "alpha", "beta", "basis")],
             digits = 5, caption = "PSA distributions")

# Test function to generate PSA input dataset
generate_psa_params(n_sim = 10) 

## Generate PSA dataset 
# Number of simulations
n_sim <- 1000

# Generate PSA input dataset
df_psa_input <- generate_psa_params(n_sim = n_sim, params_basecase = l_params_all)
# First six observations
head(df_psa_input)

### Histogram of parameters 
ggplot(melt(df_psa_input, variable.name = "Parameter"), aes(x = value)) +
  facet_wrap(~Parameter, scales = "free") +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density))) +
  ylab("") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 16) + 
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 6),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank()) 
```

## 11.2 Run PSA

```{r}
# Initialize data.frames with PSA output 
# data.frame of costs
df_c <- as.data.frame(matrix(0, 
                             nrow = n_sim,
                             ncol = n_str))
colnames(df_c) <- v_names_str
# data.frame of effectiveness
df_e <- as.data.frame(matrix(0, 
                             nrow = n_sim,
                             ncol = n_str))
colnames(df_e) <- v_names_str

# Conduct probabilistic sensitivity analysis
# Run Markov model on each parameter set of PSA input dataset
n_time_init_psa_series <- Sys.time()
for (i in 1:n_sim) { # i <- 1
  l_psa_input <- update_param_list(l_params_all, as.list(df_psa_input[i,]))
  # Outcomes
  l_out_ce_temp  <- calculate_ce_out(l_psa_input)
  df_c[i, ]  <- l_out_ce_temp$Cost  
  df_e[i, ]  <- l_out_ce_temp$Effect
  # Display simulation progress
  if (i/(n_sim/100) == round(i/(n_sim/100), 0)) { # display progress every 5%
    cat('\r', paste(i/n_sim * 100, "% done", sep = " "))
  }
}
n_time_end_psa_series <- Sys.time()
n_time_total_psa_series <- n_time_end_psa_series - n_time_init_psa_series
print(paste0("PSA with ", scales::comma(n_sim), " simulations run in series in ", 
             round(n_time_total_psa_series, 2), " ", 
             units(n_time_total_psa_series)))
```

# 11.3 Visualize PSA results for CEA

```{r}
### Create PSA object 
l_psa <- make_psa_obj(cost          = df_c, 
                      effectiveness = df_e, 
                      parameters    = df_psa_input, 
                      strategies    = v_names_str)
l_psa$strategies <- v_names_str
colnames(l_psa$effectiveness) <- v_names_str
colnames(l_psa$cost) <- v_names_str

# Vector with willingness-to-pay (WTP) thresholds.
v_wtp <- seq(0, 150000, by = 5000)
```

## 11.3.1 Cost-Effectiveness Scatter plot

```{r}
### Cost-Effectiveness Scatter plot 
txtsize <- 13
gg_scattter <- plot_psa(l_psa, txtsize = txtsize) +
  ggthemes::scale_color_colorblind() +
  ggthemes::scale_fill_colorblind() +
  scale_y_continuous("Cost (Thousand $)", 
                     breaks = number_ticks(10),
                     labels = function(x) x/1000) +
  xlab("Effectiveness (QALYs)") +
  guides(col = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
gg_scattter
```

### 11.3.1b Incremental cost-effectiveness plane with WTP line (addition)

```{r ce-plane-incremental}
# plot_psa() above shows ABSOLUTE costs and QALYs of each strategy, so a
# willingness-to-pay line cannot be drawn on it. Here each PSA draw is one
# point: transplant minus dialysis.
n_wtp_plane <- 50000                                    # $ per QALY
df_inc_psa <- data.frame(inc_qaly = df_e[[v_names_str[2]]] - df_e[[v_names_str[1]]],
                         inc_cost = df_c[[v_names_str[2]]] - df_c[[v_names_str[1]]])
# Cost-effective at the threshold = point lies below the WTP line
# (inc_cost < WTP x inc_qaly), i.e. incremental NMB > 0
df_inc_psa$cost_effective <- df_inc_psa$inc_cost < n_wtp_plane * df_inc_psa$inc_qaly

# Share of draws in each quadrant and below the line
v_share <- c(
  cost_effective_at_WTP = mean(df_inc_psa$cost_effective),
  dominant              = mean(df_inc_psa$inc_cost < 0 & df_inc_psa$inc_qaly > 0),  # cheaper and better (SE quadrant)
  more_costly_better    = mean(df_inc_psa$inc_cost > 0 & df_inc_psa$inc_qaly > 0),  # NE quadrant
  cheaper_worse         = mean(df_inc_psa$inc_cost < 0 & df_inc_psa$inc_qaly < 0),  # SW quadrant
  dominated             = mean(df_inc_psa$inc_cost > 0 & df_inc_psa$inc_qaly < 0))  # NW quadrant
round(v_share, 3)

gg_plane <- ggplot(df_inc_psa, aes(x = inc_qaly, y = inc_cost)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = cost_effective), alpha = 0.4, size = 1.2) +
  stat_ellipse(level = 0.95, type = "norm", linewidth = 0.8) +    # 95% confidence ellipse
  geom_point(aes(x = mean(inc_qaly), y = mean(inc_cost)), size = 3, shape = 4) +  # mean
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = n_wtp_plane, linetype = "dashed") +           # WTP line
  annotate("label", x = max(df_inc_psa$inc_qaly), y = n_wtp_plane * max(df_inc_psa$inc_qaly),
           label = "WTP = $50,000/QALY", hjust = 1, size = 3.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#1F7A8C", `FALSE` = "#E08E0B"),
                      labels = c(`TRUE` = "Cost-effective", `FALSE` = "Not cost-effective"),
                      name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(x = "Incremental QALYs (transplant vs dialysis)",
       y = "Incremental cost (transplant vs dialysis)",
       title = "Incremental cost-effectiveness plane, ECD/DCD transplant vs continued dialysis") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = range(c(df_inc_psa$inc_cost, 0, n_wtp_plane * max(df_inc_psa$inc_qaly))),   # include the top of the WTP line so its label shows
                  xlim = range(c(df_inc_psa$inc_qaly, 0))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
gg_plane
```

## 11.3.2 Incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) with probabilistic output

```{r}
### Incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) with probabilistic output 
# Compute expected costs and effects for each strategy from the PSA
df_out_ce_psa <- summary(l_psa)
df_cea_psa <- calculate_icers(cost       = df_out_ce_psa$meanCost, 
                              effect     = df_out_ce_psa$meanEffect,
                              strategies = df_out_ce_psa$Strategy)
df_cea_psa
```

## 11.3.3 Plot cost-effectiveness frontier with probabilistic output

```{r}
### Plot cost-effectiveness frontier with probabilistic output 
plot_icers(df_cea_psa, label = "all", txtsize = txtsize) +
  expand_limits(x = max(table_cea$QALYs) + 0.1) +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.8, 0.3))
```

## 11.3.4 Cost-effectiveness acceptability curves (CEACs) and frontier (CEAF)

```{r}
### Cost-effectiveness acceptability curves (CEACs) and frontier (CEAF) 
ceac_obj <- ceac(wtp = v_wtp, psa = l_psa)
# Regions of highest probability of cost-effectiveness for each strategy
summary(ceac_obj)
# CEAC & CEAF plot
gg_ceac <- plot_ceac(ceac_obj, txtsize = txtsize, xlim = c(0, NA), n_x_ticks = 14) +
  ggthemes::scale_color_colorblind() +
  ggthemes::scale_fill_colorblind() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.8, 0.48))
gg_ceac
```

## 11.3.5 Expected Loss Curves (ELCs)

```{r}
### Expected Loss Curves (ELCs) 
elc_obj <- calc_exp_loss(wtp = v_wtp, psa = l_psa)
elc_obj

# ELC plot
gg_elc <- plot_exp_loss(elc_obj, log_y = FALSE, 
               txtsize = txtsize, xlim = c(0, NA), n_x_ticks = 14,
               col = "full") +
  ggthemes::scale_color_colorblind() +
  ggthemes::scale_fill_colorblind() +
  # geom_point(aes(shape = as.name("Strategy"))) +
  scale_y_continuous("Expected Loss (Thousand $)", 
                     breaks = number_ticks(10),
                     labels = function(x) x/1000) +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.4, 0.7),)
gg_elc
```

## 11.3.6 Expected value of perfect information (EVPI)

```{r}
### Expected value of perfect information (EVPI) 
evpi <- calc_evpi(wtp = v_wtp, psa = l_psa)
# EVPI plot
gg_evpi <- plot_evpi(evpi, effect_units = "QALY", 
                     txtsize = txtsize, xlim = c(0, NA), n_x_ticks = 14) +
  scale_y_continuous("EVPI (Thousand $)", 
                     breaks = number_ticks(10),
                     labels = function(x) x/1000)
gg_evpi
```
